messages:
anya: heads-up — running into noisy churn from reservation heartbeats when tenants have sporadic bursts. pin+heartbeat model is causing short-lived evictions and cold KV cache thrash. thinking about suppressing heartbeats while a reservation is occupied by inflight vectors. any immediate objections?

sam: can you sketch the lifecycle you're imagining? not sure I follow how suppression avoids races with admission.

anya: sure. current flow: lease(reservation) acquired -> periodic heartbeat refresh every 1s -> lease TTL extends; when client traffic pauses, heartbeat keeps lease alive which blocks others. idea: when a reservation has active inflight batches (>=1), stop sending periodic heartbeats. only start a suppression-timer when inflight drops to 0; if no new arrivals in suppression window (e.g., 250ms), then send renew; otherwise skip. reduces churn for bursty tenants.

keith: hmmm. main risk is fairness: if tenant keeps streaming tiny requests, they effectively hold slot forever without paying the heartbeat cost, which is fine, but could starve a waiting tenant in steady-state. how do we bound that?

maria: agree with keith. we need two knobs: max-contiguous-hold (absolute time a single tenant can keep reservation via continuous inflight) and a soft-evict-after metric that allows safe preemption. also add telemetry for per-reservation hold-time and waiters.

anya: yep. propose these knobs: "suppression_window_ms": 250, "max_hold_ms": 30_000, "soft_preempt_threshold_ms": 10000. soft preempt attempts graceful drain on next batch boundary.

cj (typo -> tj): pseudo code for suppression:

```
on_inflight = 0
on_inflight_timer = null
on_inflight_timer_on_expiry: send_renew()

on_batch_start(): non_inflight += 1; if non_inflight_timer != null: cancel(non_inflight_timer)
on_batch_end(): non_inflight -= 1; if non_inflight == 0: non_inflight_timer = set_timer(suppression_window_ms)

periodic_heartbeat() {
  // only if reservation idle for > suppression_window_ms OR force_renew flag set
}
```

tj: love it. edge cases: streaming with intermittent keep-alive (websocket/csi) — treat open stream as inflight. also we need to handle host restarts where heartbeat broker missed a tick. so lease TTL must be > suppression_window + jitter.

keith: question about admission: if we suppress heartbeats while inflight, the scheduler's view might mark slot as expiring and attempt a provisional admission for another tenant, causing contention. do we need a separate "pin-present" signal separate from the lease TTL that admission checks?

anya: exactly. propose a two-layer signal: short-lived runtime pin (in-memory, authoritative on the server that holds the reservation) + lease in control-plane for durability. admission first consults runtime pin, then falls back to lease TTL. that avoids racing on the control-plane heartbeat window.

maria: that means the runtime needs to replicate pin state to local schedulers and expose an API: isPinned(reservationId) -> bool. cheap-to-check and eventually consistent is fine for fast path. but we must handle scheduler restarts losing in-memory pin. have fallback to control-plane lease with longer TTL (e.g., 60s).

anya: yes. we can make the lease TTL 60s, heartbeat envelope 1s normally, but suppression means no heartbeat while active. runtime pin TTL could be 2s from last inflight activity and refreshed by in-process events.

infra-bot: deploy scheduled: heartbeat-suppression feature-flag will be rolled to alpha on canary-3 at 2026-04-01T09:00Z :robot_face:

sam: what metrics to watch in the alpha? my list: reservation-evictions/sec, average-queue-wait-ms, tail-99.9-latency, kvcache-miss-rate-per-tenant, soft-preempt-count. also add a gauge for runtime-pin-misses (cases admission checked runtime pin and it was absent).

maria: add per-tenant fairness index: fraction of time tenant occupied while others waited. we'll need to baseline.

keith: and add a histogram for suppression-window-expiries (how often we renew vs skip).

anya: plan: I'll prototype on canary, expose flags: suppression_window_ms, max_hold_ms, runtime_pin_ttl_ms. then run A/B vs control for 48h. if eviction rate down and tail latency <= baseline, we can roll. creating RFC follow-up doc after experiment results.

tj: also include unit test for race: simulate tenant A finishes inflight -> suppressed timer scheduled -> almost-simultaneous tenant B admission request. verify admission path checks runtime pin then lease TTL and doesn't double-allocate.

anya: ok capturing action items: 1) anya protos + PR to canary 2) testing plan + metrics dashboard (sam/maria) 3) race unit tests (tj/keith) 4) RFC follow-up draft after 48h. anyone want to add? :rocket:

keith: add a stress test w/ streaming tiny requests to validate max_hold_ms enforcement.

sam: +1, will own dashboards.

anya: thanks all — will ping when PR is up.
